# Tab 2.1 \- It's Principles

let's start with big things: Celestial bodies

Big bodies have a big mass, and so give a lot of gravity.  
Gravity is a force, a push (it's what keeps you to the ground\! and makes airplanes pricey) and in cosmonautics we want to cancel it all out with thrust, or lift, but lift requires air and also gives out drag.  
Thrust is produced by rocket engines (without air) or by propellers (with air).  
If you're never going to leave the atmosphere (and don't go to supersonic speeds\*) a propeller is recommended. If you're going over the atmosphere, a rocket engine is REQUIRED as they don't need the atmosphere.  
Except if you're that one tesla in space1, don't ask me how it reached that place, it's funnier if i don't tell you.  
Lesson finished. What was it about? the four forces of Newton, they're that simple.

![][image2]  
¹ a car in space.

\*In real life, some jet engines can go supersonic and need air\! Example is the Concorde.

# The Sputnik

The Sputnik is by far the most complicated part of the Cosmonautics mod, but luckily it's concept is pretty easy to understand and you won't require highly complicated code for most of your rockets, and a high number of programs within the sputnik won't be necessary for flight. For example: The Audio functions.

This guide will cover most if not all of the functions needed for flight, and if I (or someone else) completes the functions, I'll also start with the others.

# Adding interactability

This lesson will be short.

When you want to do fun stuff like activating a light bulb, you don’t short out two electric poles manually by opening an electrical box, instead you use a switch, which is an input.  
We have two possibilities for a switch, a toggle switch inside a Sputnik, or a Redstone level, and connecting it with the sputnik via a “Redstone Link Receiver" block.  
In the image, there’s also two constants as inputs, and a button trigger which when clicked emits a pulse, if you hold it, nothing happens.  
![][image21]

An input is used to change an output, so let’s add outputs![][image22]  
I’ve also customized the inputs a little.

# Complex logic

There are only five logic blocks that don’t only use 1 or 0, those are:  
Timer, Select, Memory, Compare and PID Controller

The timer block is a clock, it waits until an amount of time has passed (*Run*) and then it ticks (it sends a pulse to the *Seconds* output) and then starts to count again.  
To send it back to counting from zero you have to do what you can’t do on a normal clock, but in coding terms, you have to send a pulse to the *Reset* input.

This is the timer’s code:![][image23]

Next up is the Select block.  
it says what it does in the code. Here it is:![][image24]

Next up is the Memory block\! and it’s explained already in code![][image25]

Next up is the Compare block. Pretty intuitive by image.![][image26]

Next is the PID controller.	(thanks to @tomqnto on discord for the explanation\!)  
![][image27]  
*“don’t use ki.”* \-tomqnto

in the *SetPoint* input, send the value you want to reach.  
in the *ProcessValue* input, send the value you are in.  
Kp and Kd are basically sensitivity values. kP (proportional gain) determines how strongly the system reacts to the current error. (high kP results in a larger correction, which could result in over correction, a lower kP results in a lower correction, which could result in an undercorrection). Kd instead determines how strongly the system reacts to the rate of change of error (a larger kD helps the system prevent overshooting and if it’s too low there’s an overshoot).

# Sputnik \- Lua

This Section describes the function and uses of the Sputnik via lua code.  
Differently from the upper Sputnik chapter ([Cosmonautics: a documentation.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tfDjDsqYeB11w_2OHdxhIqd2glCQg05Vt4aJTNIRpcc/edit?tab=t.1xpn1a2aau7i) ) this chapter won’t in any way show code in the form of coding blocks (except for some cases).

# What is Lua?

Lua is a coding language whose name comes from the portuguese word for moon, “Lua”.  
Lua is used by games and programs. An example is League of Legends and Roblox (even though they use a dialect of Lua, Luau, made by Roblox Inc.).  
Differently from Java, Python and C languages, Lua is vastly simpler to use, however it does not work directly to and from the Cpu, instead it uses a decompiler to talk to the Cpu (and gpu), which results in less performance, hence so why it isn’t so vastly used.  
Like Roblox, the Holly Cosmonautics developers for the Sputnik have made a decompiler for Lua, however the decompiler for us is in Java, not C. The only presence of C language in the Cosm. mod is for the shaders, in the dialect named GLSL. For now, I won’t cover it.

# Tab 8 \- fixing the interactability

At the time of writing, there is a known bug where the Sputnik’s inputs that can be easily modified get set to nothing (e.g. the Redstone Link Receiver, when the Sputnik is reloaded, gets its signal frequencies nullified, and most importantly all constants do the same by turning to zero.)  
![][image28]

For now, to fix this bug, you have to modify the blocks by yourself in lua, but it’s pretty easy because of how the blocks are set up.  
I’ll use an adder block as an example for all blocks, then I’ll show the special exception of the redstone link blocks.  
Display blocks’s lua code CANNOT be edited.  
Open the adder lua code by double clicking it.![][image29]  
Here, you can see the code.  
Modify the input of what used to be for a constant, with the value or number you need

![][image30]

Exit with Esc  
You will see that there will be no input B, this is because inputs are created thanks to the *output()* function in the code.  
![][image31]

It works.![][image32]

To fix Redstone Link blocks, there’s a different but similar approach, open the block.  
![][image33]

Put in the names of the items you want just like how you would get it via /give.  
![][image34]

![][image35]  
might as well delete the other USELESS code.

yay, it works, ignore the dooplegangers.![][image36]

You can also use a Lua Script block and copy paste the code of the fixed block into the lua block, as it will be cleaner.
